page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance presents 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 105 MB of shared L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It includes 16 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced single-thread throughput alongside constrained multi-threaded scaling due to its 2 physical core count and burstable CPU allocation. Single-core performance registered 1880.68 on stress-ng and 1892.0 on Geekbench, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving a strong 32.91 GB/s and text processing scoring 2498.0. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks placed in the lower quartiles, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 3944.96, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4435.0, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 12.0 GB/s. Memory throughput tests showed 26.17 GB/s for large uncached reads and 28.03 GB/s for writes, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations reached 2063.13 and 5.08 million operations per second, respectively.

The m7i-flex.xlarge offers an economical footprint for workloads that do not fully saturate 4 vCPUs continuously. By utilizing burstable CPU scheduling, it balances operational costs for mid-tier resource demands against lower multi-threaded sustained execution limits. Primary target workloads include static web serving, light-to-moderate API backends, text processing pipelines, microservices, and general-purpose development tasks that do not depend on high sustained multicore utilization or local high-speed disk storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing a burstable CPU model on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz, the instance incorporates 16 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It includes support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero discrete GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates capable single-threaded capabilities, notably in text processing and gzip compression, while multi-threaded performance shows expected limitations under sustained loads due to physical core limits and shared burstable allocations. The instance represents a cost-effective compute platform for standard web serving, text parsing, background workers, and lightweight microservices with intermittent utilization profiles.
